1438: The location × variety interaction was significant. The highest single combination was Gobindabhog at Birbhum/Howrah with 0.5973 mg/100 mg and the lowest Radhunipagal at Purba Bardhaman with 0.0007 mg/100 mg. Since the determination was confined to fresh grain, storage terms do not arise.
1447: Tyrosine is an aromatic amino acid. It serves as the precursor of several signalling compounds and of the pigment melanin, and in plants it initiates the biosynthesis of a range of phenolic compounds. The three locations lay within 0.0014 mg/100 mg of one another and the effect was non-significant. Gobindabhog contained the most tyrosine at 0.5965 mg/100 mg, followed by Kalojira at 0.2467, while Radhunipagal again registered a trace value of 0.0014 mg/100 mg. As with cysteine, the near-absence in Radhunipagal is sufficiently extreme to warrant verification against the raw output before being reported as a genuine finding. Jayaprakash et al. (2022) reported a range of 0.81 to 6.0% for tyrosine in milled rice, so a wide varietal spread is to be expected; the spread recorded here is wider still.
1451: The effect of location on the valine content of freshly harvested grain was non-significant, the three locations returning closely comparable values: Birbhum/Howrah recorded 0.3459 mg/100 mg, Purba Bardhaman 0.3456 mg/100 mg and Nadia 0.3448 mg/100 mg.
1453: Marked differences emerged between landraces, the varietal effect being highly significant. Gobindabhog ranked highest at 0.4772 mg/100 mg, followed by Radhunipagal at 0.3316 mg/100 mg, with Kalojira lowest at 0.2276 mg/100 mg.
1455: Location and variety did not interact significantly, indicating uniform landrace behaviour across the three locations. The highest single combination was Gobindabhog at Purba Bardhaman with 0.4787 mg/100 mg and the lowest Kalojira at Purba Bardhaman with 0.2275 mg/100 mg. Storage was not sampled for this character, so no term involving it is reported.
1464: Valine is an essential branched-chain amino acid which, together with leucine and isoleucine, is utilised directly by muscle for energy and repair. The three locations differed by 0.0011 mg/100 mg, a non-significant margin. Gobindabhog contained 0.4772 mg/100 mg, Radhunipagal 0.3316 and Kalojira 0.2276 mg/100 mg, Gobindabhog thus carrying 110% more than Kalojira. Since valine is essential and must be obtained from the diet, this difference carries practical value where rice constitutes the greater part of protein intake. Sui et al. (2023) mapped the genes controlling branched-chain amino acid content in 422 rice accessions and determined the trait to be governed by many genes of small effect, which is consistent with the stable varietal differences observed here. The interaction was non-significant, the extremes being Gobindabhog at Purba Bardhaman with 0.4787 mg/100 mg and Kalojira at the same location with 0.2275 mg/100 mg.
1468: The effect of location on the isoleucine content of freshly harvested grain was non-significant, the three locations returning closely comparable values: Purba Bardhaman recorded 0.2113 mg/100 mg, Birbhum/Howrah 0.2111 mg/100 mg and Nadia 0.2104 mg/100 mg.
1470: The three landraces differed distinctly, the varietal effect attaining the 1% level. Gobindabhog carried the highest quantity, 0.2874 mg/100 mg, followed by Radhunipagal at 0.2108 mg/100 mg, with the lowest quantity recorded in Kalojira at 0.1345 mg/100 mg.
1472: The location × variety interaction was significant. The highest single combination was Gobindabhog at Birbhum/Howrah with 0.2883 mg/100 mg and the lowest Kalojira at Purba Bardhaman with 0.1340 mg/100 mg. This parameter was determined in fresh grain only, so no storage interaction is reported.
1481: Isoleucine is the second of the three essential branched-chain amino acids. It supports muscle repair, contributes to the regulation of blood glucose and participates in haemoglobin formation. The three locations lay within 0.0009 mg/100 mg of one another and the effect was non-significant. Gobindabhog contained 0.2874 mg/100 mg, Radhunipagal 0.2108 and Kalojira 0.1345 mg/100 mg. Isoleucine was the least abundant of the three branched-chain amino acids in all three landraces, which is the customary pattern in cereal protein; Sui et al. (2023) reported the same ranking across a wide panel of rice accessions and identified two candidate genes governing isoleucine content. The interaction was significant — the second of only two amino acids for which this obtained — although the ranking of the landraces was conserved at all three locations.
1485: The effect of location on the leucine content of freshly harvested grain was non-significant, the three locations returning closely comparable values: Nadia recorded 0.4069 mg/100 mg, Birbhum/Howrah 0.4062 mg/100 mg and Purba Bardhaman 0.4057 mg/100 mg.
1487: Distinct differences separated the landraces, the varietal effect being highly significant. The largest quantity occurred in Gobindabhog at 0.5502 mg/100 mg, followed by Radhunipagal with 0.4060 mg/100 mg, while Kalojira carried the least at 0.2625 mg/100 mg.
1489: The interaction being non-significant, the landraces responded identically at each of the three locations. The highest single combination was Gobindabhog at Birbhum/Howrah with 0.5523 mg/100 mg and the lowest Kalojira at Purba Bardhaman with 0.2618 mg/100 mg. No storage samples were assayed for this character; storage interactions are therefore not reported.
1498: Leucine is the third and most metabolically active of the branched-chain amino acids. It constitutes the strongest dietary stimulus to muscle protein synthesis and contributes to the regulation of blood glucose. The three locations lay within 0.0012 mg/100 mg of one another and the effect was non-significant. Gobindabhog contained 0.5502 mg/100 mg, Radhunipagal 0.4060 and Kalojira 0.2625 mg/100 mg. Leucine was the most abundant of the three branched-chain amino acids in every landrace, which accords with the general composition of cereal protein and with the wide panel of accessions examined by Sui et al. (2023). Gobindabhog carried 110% more than Kalojira. The interaction was non-significant and the ranking was conserved at every location, the extremes being Gobindabhog at Birbhum and Howrah with 0.5523 mg/100 mg and Kalojira at Purba Bardhaman with 0.2618 mg/100 mg.
1502: The effect of location on the phenylalanine content of freshly harvested grain was non-significant, the three locations returning closely comparable values: Birbhum/Howrah recorded 0.2426 mg/100 mg, Nadia 0.2404 mg/100 mg and Purba Bardhaman 0.2403 mg/100 mg.
1504: The landraces differed distinctly, the varietal effect being highly significant. Gobindabhog ranked highest with 0.3598 mg/100 mg, Radhunipagal occupied second position at 0.2301 mg/100 mg and Kalojira the last at 0.1333 mg/100 mg.
1506: No significant location × variety interaction arose, each landrace therefore behaving comparably at all three sites. The highest single combination was Gobindabhog at Birbhum/Howrah with 0.3626 mg/100 mg and the lowest Kalojira at Nadia with 0.1324 mg/100 mg. Since the determination was confined to fresh grain, storage terms do not arise.
1515: Phenylalanine is an essential aromatic amino acid. The phenolic compounds of the grain are elaborated from it, so the two sets of results taken together suggest that Kalojira diverts a greater proportion of its phenylalanine into phenolic biosynthesis rather than accumulating the amino acid itself. The ranking of the three landraces for amino acids corresponds to their ranking for soluble protein, Gobindabhog leading both the others. Sui et al. (2023) likewise determined grain amino acid content to be strongly genotype-dependent in a panel of 422 rice accessions. This pattern is characteristic of cereal grain, the principal storage protein of rice being rich in this amino acid. The two sets of results are mutually consistent and support the contention of Itani et al. (2004) that locational differences in aroma are traceable to the quantity of precursor available during grain filling.
1517: The analysis of variance reported in sections 4.1 to 4.7 treats each parameter in isolation. That approach establishes whether a given factor altered a given trait, but it cannot indicate how the traits covary or which treatments are alike in overall profile. Three further analyses were therefore undertaken to address those questions: correlation analysis, principal component analysis and hierarchical cluster analysis.
1518: All three were based on the thirty six location × variety × storage treatment means, pooled over the two years, for the twenty three parameters in which storage was assayed. The fifteen amino acids were excluded, having been determined in fresh grain alone and therefore being unavailable for all thirty six treatments. It should be borne in mind that these analyses employ treatment means rather than individual replicate values, so that the coefficients describe the covariation of treatment means and do not constitute estimates of correlation among individual observations.
1519: The multivariate approach adopted here follows current practice. Abdelsalam et al. (2025) combined physical, cooking, nutritional and micronutrient characters of rice cultivars within a single principal component and cluster analysis and demonstrated that the integrated profile discriminates cultivars more reliably than any single trait, which is the rationale for grouping the treatment combinations on all characters jointly in the present study.
1521: The thirty six treatment means were used to determine the covariation of the twenty three quality parameters. Pearson correlation coefficients were computed for all 253 possible pairs. With 36 pairs of values and 34 degrees of freedom, a coefficient of 0.329 or greater is significant at the 5% level and one of 0.424 or greater at the 1% level. Eighty seven of the 253 pairs, or 34%, exceeded the 5% threshold. The full matrix is presented in Figure 4.1, in which only the significant coefficients are printed.
1522: The strongest association of all obtained between total phenol and total flavonoid, at r = +0.966. This approaches a one-to-one relationship and is precisely what the chemistry predicts, flavonoids constituting one family within the phenolic group and being enumerated twice, once in each assay. In practical terms one of the two determinations therefore carries almost no information absent from the other, and a laboratory constrained for time could measure either alone with negligible loss.
1523: Total phenol was likewise strongly associated with antioxidant capacity at r = +0.896, and flavonoid with antioxidant capacity at r = +0.888. These three together constitute a tightly cohering block. Since the phenolic compounds of the grain perform the greater part of the antioxidant function, a landrace or location rich in one will be rich in all three.
1524: Aroma correlated with fat at r = +0.894, which ranks among the more instructive findings to emerge from the correlation analysis. Both declined by approximately one third over the year, and did so in concert, treatment by treatment. This corroborates the argument advanced in section 4.3 that the two are causally linked, the products of lipid breakdown imparting the stale odour of old rice and acting antagonistically to whatever aroma persists. Aroma was further correlated with antioxidant capacity at r = +0.854 and with phenol at r = +0.796, so that the entire complex of desirable qualities rises and falls as a unit.
1525: The strongest negative association obtained between amylose and soluble protein at r = -0.886. Starch and protein compete for the same space within the endosperm, so grain rich in one tends to be poor in the other. Chattopadhyay et al. (2018) reported the same negative association between grain protein and amylose in rice. Amylose was also negatively correlated with antioxidant capacity at r = -0.749 and with fat at r = -0.687, amylose having increased during storage while these two declined.
1526: Among the minerals, copper and manganese were negatively associated at r = -0.764, while copper and zinc were positively associated at r = +0.685. Copper and zinc are absorbed by partially shared routes within the plant, which accounts for the positive association, whereas manganese behaves differently, its availability being so strongly contingent upon the degree of flooding and reduction of the soil.
1527: Two associations bear upon milling practice. Milling percentage correlated with total starch at r = +0.721 and hulling with total starch at r = +0.660: grain well filled with starch is denser and withstands polishing more effectively. Head rice recovery correlated with ash at r = +0.640, negatively with phytic acid at r = -0.540, and with moisture at r = +0.520.
1528: Considered as a whole, the correlation matrix carries an important implication for future work on these landraces. The desirable traits constitute a single tightly associated complex that declines in concert during storage — aroma, fat, phenol, flavonoid, antioxidant capacity and soluble protein — against which amylose moves inversely. A single judiciously chosen determination from within that complex, such as antioxidant capacity or aroma, would afford a reliable indication of the remainder and would economise considerable laboratory effort in a screening programme.
1532: Principal component analysis was performed on the same matrix of thirty six treatment means and twenty three parameters. Because the parameters are expressed in widely disparate units, ranging from colour readings in the hundreds to mineral concentrations in thousandths of a milligram, every parameter was first standardised to a mean of zero and a standard deviation of one. This procedure accords each parameter equal weight and prevents the larger magnitudes from dominating the outcome.
